name: Coding robot policies in simulation
description: Can a coding agent turn a task instruction into a reusable robot controller? We compare Astra and Fable on the RoboDojo benchmark.
image_alt: Simulated robot arms facing three blocks on a wooden tabletop.
summary: The coding agent develops a controller using task and interface documentation plus evaluator feedback. The selected code is then frozen and evaluated across 20 scene layouts per setting. No coding agent participates during rollout.
findings: Astra’s policies achieve 46.94% success; Fable’s achieve 42.50% across their 360-episode panels.
Both show relative strength on symbolic tasks and lose success in the base/random pairs for block stacking and cloth folding.
Neither completes coin insertion or xylophone playing in the scored panel. Failures involve perception, grasp retention and contact preparation.
limits: This is a historical comparison on a development panel, with unequal coding histories. It is not a held-out or equal-budget model ranking.

name: Agents on physical robots
description: From stacking objects to inserting an Ethernet plug: examine how agent-written code and online agent calls work together on real hardware.
image_alt: Physical robot arms holding an Ethernet cable beside a computer.
mode: Offline coding + online agent API calls
summary: The physical experiment combines offline coding with online agent API calls during execution. Each agent has five recorded trials for Ethernet insertion, Hanoi tower sorting and block stacking. This is a separate protocol from frozen-code simulation evaluation.
findings: The report records 15/15 successes for Astra and 10/15 for Fable.
Both complete all five block-stacking trials and all five hanoi tower sorting trials.
Astra completes five mechanical Ethernet insertions; Fable completes none of its five recorded insertion attempts.
limits: Ethernet success means mechanical insertion, not verified electrical connectivity. Block results score stacking, not a full stack-and-unstack cycle. Physical and simulation rates have separate denominators and are not pooled.
